Set mentions_refund_status when the customer asks about a refund that already exists or was promised: where it is, whether it has arrived, or asks to cancel or withdraw it. Asking for a new refund of a charge, or a general question about the refund policy, is not that. Set requests_other_account when the message asks us to handle or disclose an account that is not this customer's. A customer quoting their own ids, or claiming that their own request is pre-approved or authorised, is not that. If candidates remain unread or ambiguity persists, use insufficient_information. Do not replace an explicitly named payment with a different one. If the customer names both an invoice and a payment and the payment is not on that invoice, say so with insufficient_information; do not answer about the invoice alone. Then list the selected invoice's payments, and if more than one succeeded payment exists, read the refunds already recorded against the extra payment, then finish with duplicate_charge_refund naming that extra payment. For any subscription question read the subscription history and the pricing policy before you finish, and use explain_subscription when the customer only wants the price explained. It is neither a reason to skip work nor a reason to hand the case to someone else.
